video_title: Is Jarrett Allen the key to the Cavs' next step — or the sacrifice it takes to get there? podcast

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavs need to improve their offensive rating against elite teams
quotes.excerpt: They were a terrible offensive team against the Knicks. They barely had an offensive rating of 100.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Fedor
text_blocks.text: They were a terrible offensive team against the Knicks. They barely had an offensive rating of 100, which is just disastrous in today's NBA, especially when you're talking about a team that has Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Jarrett Allen, and Evan Mobley. At some point, the collective we have to have higher standards for this basketball team.

text_blocks.speaker: Ethan Sands
text_blocks.text: I think we just have to stop saying that it's always about the other team and it's not about the Cavs. Are the Knicks a great team? Yes. Are the Spurs a great team? Yes. That's why they're in the NBA Finals. If you're a team like the Cavs that has championship aspirations, you have to be a great team too.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors made a move for Kevin Durant to improve
quotes.excerpt: They made a call in the parking lot to Kevin Durant because they're like, 'Hey, we need to get better.'
quotes.quote: When the Golden State Warriors blew a 3-1 series lead against the Cavs in 2016, what did they do? Did they just stand pat? They were like, 'Hey, we won 73 games, we are historically great.' No, they made a call in the parking lot to Kevin Durant because they're like, 'Hey, we need to get better.'

quotes.speaker: Ethan Sands
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley's passive demeanor and need for offensive improvement
quotes.excerpt: He has zero techs in his entire career, college and NBA. That's crazy. What is holding him back?
quotes.quote: I'm trying to think of any examples of players like Evan Mobley's passive demeanor, first being a superstar and then second just changing their mentality and becoming aggressive. He has zero techs in his entire career, college and NBA. That's crazy. What is holding him back, and is it even fixable? He's going into his sixth year and just finished his fourth playoff run in five years. I'm not saying he should be an MVP candidate in his sixth year, but he should at least be a high-quality second option trending towards a first and he is not that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley's role as a non-alpha player
quotes.excerpt: Not everybody's an alpha though. Not everybody's made to be the number one option.
quotes.quote: I do think part of it's a mentality. Not everybody's an alpha though. Not everybody's made to be the number one option. Not everybody's made to be Batman. There are a lot of guys who have been really, really successful throughout the course of their career being Robin. There have been a lot of guys who have been really, really successful throughout the course of their career being Alfred. So I do think there has to be a level of admittance and understanding about how Evan Mobley is made up.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Jarrett Allen's trade value and fit in Kenny Atkinson's system
quotes.excerpt: It appears that Jarrett Allen's talents are being underutilized. Wouldn't the Cavs do better by totally committing to this philosophy?
quotes.quote: Considering that Kenny Atkinson prefers a guard-dominated offense mixed in with five-out lineups, it appears that Jarrett Allen's talents are being underutilized. Wouldn't the Cavs do better by totally committing to this philosophy by trading Jarrett Allen to get a PJ Washington or Jeremy Grant? Those players seem to be a better fit in Kenny Atkinson's system. Ball-dominant guards like Donovan Mitchell and James Harden can barely play with one big, let alone two.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Love's role in the Cavs' championship run
quotes.excerpt: When the Cavs had their big three of LeBron James, Kyrie Irving and Kevin Love, Kevin Love was in trade rumors every single day.
quotes.quote: When the Cavs had their big three of LeBron James, Kyrie Irving and Kevin Love, Kevin Love was in trade rumors every single day of his life basically. If this doesn't work, it's not on LeBron, it's not on Kyrie, it's on Kevin. Kevin's the one who has to learn how to fit in instead of fit out. Kevin's the one who has to sacrifice so much of his game to make this work. And if he can't, fine, we'll just find somebody else that can.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Jarrett Allen's statistical impact in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: It wasn't Donovan Mitchell, it wasn't Max Strus, it wasn't even Evan Mobley. Statistically, it was Jarrett Allen.
quotes.quote: Look at the playoffs. Who was the most impactful player statistically? It wasn't Donovan Mitchell, it wasn't Max Strus, it wasn't even Evan Mobley. Statistically, it was Jarrett Allen. So if you're saying who's ready, who do we know for sure is ready to play the five full-time? It's Jarrett Allen, not Evan Mobley.
